details: For every prime $p$, $\mathrm{Y}_p(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm{Y}_0(\mathcal H)$. For each fixed finite class, equality holds for all but finitely many primes. The only possible exceptional primes divide torsion in an integral homology group of a Hochster/interval complex. Universal coefficients do not by themselves compare two distinct positive primes, so no relationship between them is recorded here.
proof: For every integral complex $K$ in the Hochster formula, the universal coefficient exact sequence says that $\widetilde H_i(K;\mathbb F_p)$ is built from $\widetilde H_i(K;\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb F_p$ and $\operatorname{Tor}(\widetilde H_{i-1}(K;\mathbb Z),\mathbb F_p)$. A nonzero rational group has a free integral summand and therefore stays nonzero over every $\mathbb F_p$, giving $\mathrm{Y}_p\geq\mathrm{Y}_0$. There are finitely many relevant finite complexes and each has torsion at only finitely many primes, so outside their union the mod-$p$ and rational homology—and hence the Yang dimensions—agree. This does not compare two exceptional primes.
proof_source: Coefficient-field discussion and the Hochster/interval-homology formulation: ~/latex/YangDim/yang_dimension_combinatorics.tex, Section `The cube-envelope lattice and the Gasharov--Peeva--Welker formula` (unpublished local draft).
name: Characteristic-p Yang Dimension / Characteristic-zero Yang Dimension
